ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended effective 1 October 2020); Administrative Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Data Management (PBOC Order No. 1, 2022); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Enterprises (joint PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Enterprise Name Registration and Administration Measures (SAMR Order No. 26, effective 2021); Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration (State Council Order No. 746); for the Taiwan-sourced investor, the Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act and Taiwan Company Act also impose relevant UBO and record-keeping duties.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Parent (Taiwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only if the document originates in an Apostille Convention member state: notary attestation -> apostille certificate from the designated competent authority; no embassy legalization. Non-member Consular path (parallel, mutually exclusive, never sequential): notary attestation -> ministry of foreign affairs authentication -> consular legalization at the destination embassy/consulate. For Taiwan-sourced documents used in mainland China, the parallel substitute is SEF/ARATS cross-strait notarization verification; only one path may be used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Company Registration Information (Ultimate Parent, Taiwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Central or Regional Company Registration Authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only if the document originates in an Apostille Convention member state: notary attestation -> apostille certificate; no embassy legalization. Non-member Consular path (parallel, mutually exclusive, never sequential): notary attestation -> foreign affairs certificate -> consular legalization. For Taiwan-sourced documents used in mainland China, use SEF/ARATS cross-strait notarization verification as the exclusive substitute; never chain apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorising the WFOE incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan Ultimate Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (member state): notarise board resolution -> apostille by competent authority -> file directly. Non-member Consular path (parallel and exclusive): notarise board resolution -> local foreign affairs ministry certification -> legalisation by the destination consulate -> file. For Taiwan-sourced resolutions, use SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification as the sole alternate; do not apply both apostille and consular stamps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Charter of the Ultimate Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ultimate Parent company secretary / legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (member state): notarised copy -> apostille certificate -> accepted by PRC/SAMR or banking authorities where apostille treaty applies. Non-member Consular path (parallel substitute): notarised copy -> foreign ministry legalisation folder -> destination consulate visa -> accepted. For Taiwan entities, the non-consular, non-apostille SEF/ARATS notarization verification path is mandatory; the three paths are mutually exclusive and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the Ultimate Parent's banking history and creditworthiness
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in Taiwan (corporate banking branch)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (member state): bank officer attestation -> notarisation -> apostille by competent authority -> direct submission. Non-member Consular path (parallel substitute): bank officer attestation -> notarisation -> foreign affairs ministry authentication -> consular legalization -> direct submission. For Taiwan-sourced bank letters, execute SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification; never stack apostille on top of consular legalisation or vice versa.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every shareholder, director, UBO and authorised signatory must be screened before onboarding against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, OFAC non-SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, the US BIS Entity List, the EU and UK consolidated asset-freeze lists, INTERPOL Red Notices, China's list of serious dishonest enterprises published by SAMR, the PBOC Financial Intelligence Unit watchlist, and the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission AML/CFT watchlist. Any PEP hit (domestic or foreign, immediate family, close associates) triggers enhanced due diligence with senior management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, and quarterly re-screening. A confirmed sanctions hit requires a Suspicious Transaction Report to the PBOC FIU within 24 hours and refusal to onboard unless a valid OFAC/UN license is obtained. Negative news screening in Chinese, English and Taiwanese-market sources is mandatory for each UBO.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration and Administration Online Platform (integrated with the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE name must use standardized simplified Chinese characters. Enterprise names follow the four-tier statutory structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name (zihao) + industry and business descriptor + organizational form, e.g., Shanghai [Trade Name] Wine and Spirits Bonded Trading Limited Liability Company. The English name must be a faithful transliteration of the approved Chinese name, not a free translation, and may appear in parentheses on the business license. Traditional Chinese characters, Japanese kanji, Arabic numerals, Roman letters (except permitted pinyin initials) and misleading industry terms are disallowed in the Chinese trade name unless expressly approved. Phonetic pinyin transliteration is permitted for a foreign investor name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 business days of receiving a written or online rejection, the applicant must submit a Name Reconsideration Application to the same SAMR office that issued the rejection or to its examining department, attaching the proposed simplified Chinese name, pinyin transliteration, a business plan showing the bonded wine/spirits license path, evidence of lease or ownership of the physical bonded warehouse or third-party storage agreement, and letters explaining why the name is distinctive and not deceptive. The local SAMR must decide within 15 business days. If refused again, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the municipal People's Government or the next-higher SAMR within 60 days of the refusal notice, and may thereafter initiate administrative litigation before the competent People's Court within six months. To avoid delay, a fresh name reservation may be filed simultaneously in a different acceptable formulation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 4632 bonded warehouse wholesale trade company, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the registered office or tax domicile. SAMR, the tax authorities, and the General Administration of Customs require a physical operating address because bonded wine and spirits require verifiable inventory control, customs seals, and licensable storage premises. Banks conducting PBOC Order No. 1 customer due diligence will refuse account opening for a WFOE presenting only a mailbox address. A virtual office may be used solely as supplementary correspondence address, never as the statutory seat, tax address, or customs registration address. The registered office must be supported by a lease or ownership instrument for a physical location with a term exceeding one year and must be capable of receiving official process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: HIGH; estimated 80% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of registration. Checklist for inspectors: 1) verify doorplate and signage match the business license exactly; 2) confirm the legal representative or responsible manager is present or contactable on site; 3) inspect accounting and tax invoice records that must be kept physically or immediately accessible at the address; 4) inspect bonded warehouse stock, customs seals, and liquor duty-paid evidence; 5) verify original import invoices, excise tax documents, and SWIFT or bonded transfer payment records; 6) audit employee and licensing notices. Failure on any item may trigger administrative penalty, customs licence suspension, or revocation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee; statutory zero-tariff for all market entity name filings in China.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official registration fee under the Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration; mandatory zero-fee e-filing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory no-fee filing as of the 1 November 2024 effective date.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial, apostille/consular and courier tariffs; neither SAMR nor PBOC charges this fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: International law firm / corporate services provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (as consolidated and amended), Articles 2, 5, 7, 128, 129, 130, 154, 156, 161, 171, 172, 185, 203, 218, 228, 387 and 393; supplementary provisions of the Regulations for Company Registration and Certification and the Act for the Regulation of Foreign Investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (MOEA DoC) - Taiwan Company Registration Authority, with delegated local counterpart economic development bureaus for certain registration matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation (Company Act Article 387 Form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Taiwan Company Act for a limited liability company or company limited by shares; however, the paid-up share capital must be adequate for the announced business scope. For the bonded wine and spirits trade, the applicant must additionally provide a Customs performance bond or bank guarantee and, in practice, maintain paid-in capital sufficient to support the customs-bonded inventory. No blocked escrow account is required solely for the company registry, but foreign-investor capital must be remitted and deposited in a Taiwanese bank account in the Company's name and verified by a certified public accountant before final registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], A TAIWAN WHOLY FOREIGN-OWNED ENTERPRISE LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY. RESOLVED, at a meeting of the Board of Directors duly convened and held at the registered office of the Company on [●], at which a quorum of [●] directors was present, and upon motion duly made, seconded, and unanimously carried, as follows: 1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARES: That the share subscription set out in the subscribed list is hereby accepted, and the Company shall allot and issue [●] ordinary shares with par value NT$10 each, representing paid-up share capital of NT$[●], to the founding shareholders; such capital shall be deposited in the Company's capital contribution bank account in Taiwan and shall not be withdrawn except for verified establishment costs or otherwise in accordance with the Taiwan Company Act. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: That the Company establish its primary corporate operating account with [●] Bank, and the board hereby authorizes any two of the following directors, namely [●] and [●], jointly to sign checks, SWIFT/wire transfer instructions, and all bank account-operation documents; the board further approves the bankers mandate form and authorizes the Chairperson to deliver the same to the bank. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the registered office of the Company be fixed at [●], Taiwan, and the board approves the office lease/use consent agreement as the legal seat of the Company for the receipt of official notices, statutory service and maintenance of corporate records. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: That [●] be appointed as the sole director, chairperson and legal representative of the Company; that [●] be appointed as the second director and company secretary responsible for statutory filings; and that [●] be appointed as the general manager and the responsible person for the customs bonded warehouse and alcohol licensing applications. The board expressly authorizes these officers to execute all regulatory filings, sign industrial license applications, appear before the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Customs Administration, and open all required government accounts. 5. ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATION: That the certified public accountant and licensed corporate agent appointed by the board be authorized to prepare and file the official company registration forms and to obtain the Company Registration Certificate and tax registration number. All actions taken by the officers and agents to incorporate the Company, adopt the registered office, execute banking mandates and complete the bonded warehouse licensing are hereby approved, ratified and confirmed. This resolution shall be effective immediately upon adoption and shall remain in full force until revoked by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (MOEA DoC) online name inquiry system; Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs for foreign-investor approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the MOEA name database to confirm that the proposed company name is unique and not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered enterprise. For each foreign shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner, prepare and submit an investment application through the Investment Commission online portal, attaching a certified copy of the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, audited financial statements or bank reference, proposed shareholding structure, and a detailed business plan for the bonded wholesale of aged Scotch and Bordeaux wines. If the investor is a non-English jurisdiction, all corporate documents must be notarized or apostilled and translated into Chinese. Upon approval, obtain the Investment Approval Letter and preserve its validity period. Do not execute a final warehouse lease or remit capital before this approval unless the Investment Commission permits a conditional preliminary lease.
required_dossiers: MOEA company name pre-approval application
Investment Application Form F-1
Foreign investor certificate of incorporation and good standing
Audited financial statements for the preceding year
Business plan covering ISIC 4632 bonded wine and spirits wholesale
Power of attorney to the local filing agent
Notarized board resolution of the foreign investor
Copies of passports and entry permits of proposed directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA or Investment Commission issues a query or suspension, the applicant shall access the online case management system and submit curing explanations within 15 calendar days. If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, file up to three alternative names for re-screening. If the investment approval is refused, apply for administrative reconsideration or restructure the shareholding with a local co-investor authorized by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Notarize and Execute Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan notary public and the external corporate counsel engaged by the founding shareholders; final filing with MOEA DoC.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Chinese-language statutory format, including the company name, object clauses expressly covering bonded warehousing wholesale of wines and spirituous liquors, total and paid-in capital amounts, class and number of shares, board composition, registered office address, duration, and liquidation provisions. Execute the subscriber's list and the minutes of the founding shareholders' meeting, confirming all subscriptions and the allocation of directorships. The execution pages and company seal specimen must be notarized where the registry requires proof of authentic signatures, particularly for non-Taiwanese shareholders. Retain a certified English translation for auditor and foreign banking use but ensure the Chinese text is controlling for registration. The pro-forma first board resolution prepared for this transaction must be executed contemporaneously and attached as a founding document.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Subscriber's agreement and subscription list
Minutes of the founding shareholders' meeting
Pro-forma first board resolution
Statutory declaration of compliance
Certified power of attorney for the Taiwan filing agent
Notarized/seal specimen of the foreign investor
English translation of constitutional documents, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is rejected or incomplete, re-execute the signature pages before a competent notary and re-submit. If the MOEA queries the corporate object clause, amend the Articles to state explicitly 'wholesale trading and bonded warehouse storage of alcoholic beverages falling under ISIC 4632' and file a revised resolution of the subscribers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution, Bank Account Opening and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed bank in Taiwan; a Taiwan Certified Public Accountant registered with the Financial Supervisory Commission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the Company's name at a reputable Taiwan bank, providing the Investment Approval Letter, proposed directors' identification, company seal and the board resolution naming authorized signatories. Remit the paid-up share capital from the foreign investor by SWIFT wire, ensuring the remitter name is exactly the approved foreign shareholder. Deposit the funds into the corporate capital account and instruct the bank to issue a banker's certificate confirming the received amount. A Taiwan CPA must then review the bank certificate, the remittance records and the subscriber's list, and issue a Capital Verification Report under the Company Act for delivery to the registry. The capital must remain in the account until the incorporation registration is completed; any withdrawal prior to registration is limited to legitimate establishment costs and must be documented.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account application form
Investment Approval Letter from the Investment Commission
Banker's certificate of capital deposit
CPA capital verification report
Board resolution designating bank signatories
SWIFT/telegraphic transfer receipt
Articles of Incorporation and company seal specimen
Passport and ARC copies of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or regulator questions the remittance under AML/KYC rules, request the foreign investor to supply source-of-wealth letters, chain-of-funds transaction evidence and bank references, then restart the account-opening application. If the CPA refuses to issue a verification report, correct the share subscription records and obtain a corrected bank certificate before re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing, Registration Certificate and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (MOEA DoC) or the delegated city/county bureau; afterwards, the National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance for the Business Tax and Tax ID registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the official incorporation application with the MOEA registry using the prescribed online system, attaching the signed Articles of Incorporation, subscriber list, consents of the initial directors, CPA capital verification report, proof of registered office (lease or ownership deed), and the Investment Commission approval. Pay the prescribed state fee and track the administrative case until the MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate. Once the certificate is issued, return to the local National Taxation Bureau to obtain the tax identification number (GUI) and approve the use of uniform invoices (invoice registration), and file the company seal and internal accounting title. The corporate registration must also be synchronized with the Health and Labor databases where applicable, but the critical statutory action is completing the tax registration within the statutory period after the MOEA certificate.
required_dossiers: Incorporation application form signed by all initial directors
Articles of Incorporation with chop/signature
CPA capital verification report
Registered office lease or title deed with landlord consent
Director and supervisor consent letters
Investment Commission Approval Letter
State registration fee payment receipt
Compulsory corporate seal specimen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry suspends the incorporation application, use the MOEA case query system to identify the missing document or legal defect and cure within 30 calendar days. If a director is disqualified under Company Act Article 30, replace such director by a subscriber resolution and file a fresh consent. Re-submit the amended application without needing a new name reservation unless the registered name was already approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs Bonded Warehouse Licensing and Alcohol Business Accreditation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance (temporary bonded warehouse licensing); National Treasury Administration / local municipal competent authority for tobacco and alcohol wholesale registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Company Registration Certificate and tax ID, apply in writing to the Customs Administration for permission to operate a bonded warehouse exclusively for wines and spirituous liquors, submitting the warehouse layout, security plan, inventory control accounting system, segregation plan and a customs performance bond or irrevocable bank guarantee. Simultaneously file the Tobacco and Alcohol Wholesale Business Registration or application under the Tobacco and Alcohol Administration Act, providing the corporate registration certificate, responsible person identification, clean criminal record certificate, warehouse address, and the financial statements evidencing paid-in capital. For each bonded shipment, the warehouse must then follow customs electronic clearance procedures for receiving, storing, transshipping and re-exporting imported Scotch and Bordeaux wines. All physical premises must satisfy the local fire and building code requirements before the Customs Administration inspection.
required_dossiers: MOEA Company Registration Certificate and tax ID certificate
Warehouse lease or ownership certificate
Detailed warehouse floor plan and security layout
Inventory management and accounting system description
Customs performance bond or bank guarantee
Tobacco and Alcohol Administration Act application form
Fire safety equipment installation certificate
Responsible person identity and no-criminal-record certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Customs issues a deficiency notice, submit a rectification plan and re-inspection request within 30 days, including enhanced fencing, CCTV, and lock control; if the bonded warehouse license is refused, reduce the bonded area or change the warehouse location and re-file. If the alcohol wholesale accreditation is questioned, prove the corporate objects include wholesale alcoholic beverages and re-submit the corrected registry extract.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance; National Treasury Administration, Ministry of Finance (Tobacco and Alcohol Administration); Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce; and the local municipal Department of Economic Development for the bonded warehouse operational permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Bonded Warehouse License for Wine, Spirits and Alcoholic Beverages (under The Customs Bonded Warehouse Regulations) and Tobacco and Alcohol Wholesale Business Registration (under the Tobacco and Alcohol Administration Act)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For a bonded warehouse engaged only in wholesale storage and distribution of packaged wine and spirits, the operation falls under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act's designated categories for warehousing and logistics. A Class C Environmental Registration or 'Self-Registration' applies to a small or medium bonded warehouse with gross floor area below 6,000 square meters and not located in an environmentally sensitive area. If the gross floor area is 6,000 square meters or more, or the site adjoins sensitive watersheds, protected wetlands, or endangered-species habitats, a Class B Environmental Statement or a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report (Class A) is mandatory before the building occupancy certificate can be issued.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The bonded wine and spirits warehouse must not discharge process wastewater. Sanitary wastewater only may be discharged to the public sewer; if any permit is required, effluent must comply with Taiwan Effluent Water Quality Standards (pH 6.0-9.0; BOD5 not exceeding 30 mg/L; COD not exceeding 100 mg/L; SS not exceeding 30 mg/L). Air emissions from occasional alcohol vapor and cork dust shall be controlled by natural ventilation or local exhaust; if total volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from the entire facility are estimated to exceed 1.0 metric ton per year, an air pollution operating permit is required, and fugitive VOC at the property boundary must be maintained below the applicable Taiwan emission standards (typically below 100 ppm as total hydrocarbons or as specified by the local EPA office). Hazardous waste handling, including broken glass contaminated with alcohol and obsolete or off-specification spirits, must be stored in closed containers, manifest scheduled, and delivered only to licensed hazardous waste treatment facilities; the annual waste disposal record is submitted to the EPA before March 1 of the following year.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Management Certificate and Fire Safety Equipment Installation Inspection issued by the local Fire Department under the Fire Services Act, including automatic fire alarms, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and a fire safety management plan with fire drills. The warehouse must also pass a structural load inspection by a registered professional civil/structural engineer, confirming that the racking and bonded-goods storage loads do not exceed floor capacity. Occupational clearance from the Ministry of Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act is required, covering forklift operator certification, machinery inspection, racking safety, warehouse good-housekeeping, and confined-space permits if applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration (Taiwan) through the regional National Taxation Bureau for the WFOE registered office; company registration through the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) One-Stop Business Registration Portal; electronic invoice infrastructure through the MOF e-Invoice Integration Service Platform (Turnkey Service); export clearance through the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Taiwan-resident wholly foreign-owned limited liability company, the non-resident equity holder must first obtain inward investment approval from the MOEA Investment Commission; for mainland Chinese investors, specific approval under the Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Chinese Investors is required. After MOEA incorporation under the Company Act, the WFOE must file the statutory Business Registration Application with the regional National Taxation Bureau within fifteen days of commencing business and obtain a Taiwan Unified Business Number (UB Number/TIN), which serves as the VAT registration number. The applicant must submit: articles of incorporation and company registration certificate, shareholder and director identification, power of attorney for local nominee or agent, registered office lease or title evidence, alcohol wholesale license, bonded warehouse license evidence, and other relevant sector licenses. The National Taxation Bureau then activates the business tax registration and Uniform Invoice allowance; to use electronic invoices, the entity must obtain a Key Account and register the Turnkey Service endpoint with the e-Invoice Integration Service Platform. A foreign non-resident without a Taiwan permanent establishment may instead register as a non-resident enterprise taxpayer, but the WFOE structure is resident and entity-level taxed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan has no check-the-box or fiscal unity election for corporate income tax, and no hybrid mismatch pass-through election. The only relevant concession is the small-scale VAT regime (1% sales tax under TWD 200,000 monthly turnover), but a licensed wine and spirits bonded wholesale business is not eligible for that simplified scheme.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act (Business Tax Act), supplemented by the Tobacco and Alcohol Tax Act for wine and spirits products.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary registration threshold: every profit-seeking enterprise must register before making taxable supplies; TWD 200,000 per month in taxable turnover is the statutory demarcation for the simplified small-scale business VAT rate of 1%, not an exemption threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan operates a Uniform Invoice system rather than real-time continuous transaction control. There is no government-issued digital fiscal stamp. Every taxable sale must be evidenced by a Uniform Invoice (paper, electronic, or receipt-issuing machine). E-invoices must be transmitted to the MOF e-Invoice Integration Service Platform through the Key Account and Turnkey Service within the reporting periods and validation windows set by the Ministry of Finance; the platform verifies invoice numbers, issuing taxpayer ID, and QR code integrity. Export sales must be linked to the Customs Export Declaration in the tax return.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, goods exported from Taiwan customs territory are zero-rated. For this bonded wine and spirits WFOE, zero-rating applies when the bonded goods are removed from the customs-supervised bonded warehouse and exported, evidenced by an approved Customs Export Declaration, and the beneficial ownership passes to a foreign buyer. Services directly related to the export (warehousing, handling, and freight within the bonded operation) may also be zero-rated where the purpose and destination are offshore. Excess input VAT attributable to the zero-rated export operations is refundable through the regular VAT return reconciliation mechanism, but refund claims are audited before payment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) approved by Taiwan Customs, showing the goods leaving the customs territory
Customs-supervised bonded warehouse removal or transfer record evidencing the export movement
Commercial invoice and packing list for the export sale
Original bill of lading (ocean) or air waybill (air) issued to the foreign buyer or to bearer
Bank-issued Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Taiwan bank Foreign Exchange Settlement / Export Proceeds Certificate
Sales contract or purchase order, and insurance certificate, evidencing payment terms and marine or air risk transfer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating is strictly documentary. If the exporter cannot produce the customs and foreign-exchange evidence, the supply is reclassified as domestic taxable and the 5% VAT is assessed. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, fraudulent or reckless zero-rating claims may draw a penalty of up to five times the evaded VAT, plus deferred-payment interest. The Tax Collection Act allows reassessment within seven years for non-declared or fraudulent claims. The Customs Administration may also require additional duties and impose customs penalties if bond movements are misconnected; forged export declarations or false inward remittance certificates can trigger criminal liability for tax fraud and customs forgery. The VAT refund is clawed back with penalty where the export proceeds are not repatriated within the prescribed period without Central Bank approval.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), Foreign Exchange Department
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is managed under a regulated but trade-oriented convertibility framework. Current-account receipts and payments, including import/export trade settlement, commission income, and service fees, may be freely converted through designated foreign exchange banks without prior CBC approval, subject only to the CBC large-value foreign exchange reporting threshold. Capital-account flows, however, are not automatically convertible: foreign direct investment, equity subscription, shareholder loans, cross-border intercompany loans, and return of capital require prior foreign investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), followed by CBC reporting and settlement through a designated FX bank. Profit remittance, classified as a current-account item under Taiwan rules, is generally permitted once the statutory annual audited financial statements are filed, a corporate income tax clearance is obtained, and a board resolution supporting the remittance is executed; nevertheless, for a China-parented Taiwan WFOE, the remittance must also satisfy China's SAFE profit-repatriation requirements on the receiving side. Export proceeds must be repatriated within 180 days of the export declaration; no fixed percentage is required to be converted into NT$ because the full amount may be kept in a designated foreign currency deposit account, but the underlying CBC declaration must still be completed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBC Foreign Exchange Declaration and Registration Regulations and the Foreign Trade Act, export proceeds must be collected and repatriated into Taiwan within 180 days from the date of customs export declaration. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; the exporter may retain the full proceeds in a designated Foreign Currency Deposit Account at a licensed FX bank. If the proceeds are not received within the 180-day window, the exporter must apply for an extension with documentary proof before the expiry; otherwise the bank will report non-compliance to the CBC. For bonded warehouse re-exports, the same timeline applies upon final customs exit; domestic bonded transfers do not create an export FX settlement event.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account (NTD/USD)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Mega International Commercial Bank Co., Ltd.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account with Foreign Currency Deposit Account for bonded trade settlement
Operational Current Account and Trade Finance Account (NTD and multi-currency)
Capital and Operational FX Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low - not legally viable for direct fund holding or clearing. Under the Taiwan Banking Act and the Electronic Payment Institution Act, an offshore fintech EMI that is not registered as a foreign bank branch or licensed electronic payment institution with the Financial Supervisory Commission and the CBC may not open a New Taiwan dollar corporate account, may not access local clearing systems such as FISC/CHIPS, and may not provide trade settlement services for bonded wine/spirits transactions. An offshore EMI can only function as a white-label technology interface in front of a licensed Taiwan Tier-1 bank, which still requires full onshore KYC, AML, and FX reporting obligations. Accordingly, no fintech EMI is recommended in the account structure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory responsible person and the ultimate beneficial owner of the WFOE must complete direct identity verification before account activation. In-branch physical appearance is the default requirement under FSC AML regulations. Some Tier-1 banks permit a live remote video interview for a non-resident director, provided the director's passport is certified, the corporate registry documents are notarized/apostilled, and a Taiwan-resident authorized signatory with a notarized power of attorney attends the bank in person. Remote consular proxy opening without any direct interview of the responsible person is not accepted by bank compliance committees for a China-parented Taiwan WFOE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner opacity and nominee-shareholder pattern in a China-parented Taiwan WFOE, making source of funds unclear.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized and apostilled shareholder register of the China parent; SAFE ODI filing record and the corresponding outward remittance statement; passport or national ID copies of all natural-person shareholders above 10%; a signed UBO declaration; an organization chart covering the Taiwan WFOE and China parent; board resolutions appointing the Taiwan directors; bank statements supporting the source of the capital contribution; and the MOEA Investment Commission foreign investment approval letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags in bonded wine/spirits, including over/under-invoicing, fictitious inventory, and abuse of bonded warehouse privileges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble purchase orders and pro-forma invoices from the Scotch exporter in the UK and the Bordeaux chateaux in France; independent third-party valuation reports for high-value vintage stock; Taiwan customs import declarations and CBC foreign exchange import/export declarations; item-level bonded warehouse receipts with lot and case codes; marine and all-risk cargo insurance certificates; full shipping sets (bill of lading, packing list, truck waybill); annual physical inventory and audit reports from a licensed CPA; the corresponding SWIFT MT103/MT700 payment evidence; and a compliance undertaking on no bonded-to-regular conversion without customs approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, denied-party exposure, and origin/concealment risk involving Chinese shareholders, Taiwan directors, UK Scotch, and French Bordeaux supply chains.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver transaction-level sanctions screening results from World-Check, Dow Jones, or Refinitiv for all directors, shareholders, counterparties, and suppliers; country-of-origin certificates and EU/UK export declarations for each shipment; end-user/distributor agreements; a written supply-chain declaration that no goods transship through embargoed or restricted territories; CBC foreign exchange transaction declarations; and documentary evidence of product provenance from the distillery or chateau including vintage, lot, and chain-of-custody forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient physical and economic substance for a bonded warehouse wholesale entity, creating tax-evasion and shell-company typology risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a Taiwan corporate income tax clearance certificate; the bonded warehouse license or the MOEA/FSC-approved warehouse permit; the warehouse lease agreement, utility bills, payroll records, and staffing contracts; fire safety and bonded storage certifications; audited financial statements of the Taiwan WFOE; VAT and foreign income tax filings; photos or video of the active warehouse; and the CPA capital verification report after initial capital injection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the initial equity injection from the China parent to the Taiwan WFOE's capital escrow account at a Tier-1 Taiwan bank using SWIFT MT103/MT202 with gpi tracking. Field 70 must reference the MOEA Investment Commission approval number, the CBC inbound remittance declaration number, and the foreign exchange purpose code of 'Foreign Direct Investment - Capital Subscription'. Before remittance, complete China's SAFE ODI filing and the Taiwan CBC 'inward remittance for foreign investment' declaration. After receipt, appoint a Taiwan CPA to issue the capital verification report; only then may the funds be transferred to the operating currency account or converted to New Taiwan dollars at the onshore spot rate. The capital escrow balance cannot be used for operating expenses until verification is completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier payments for Scotch and Bordeaux wine imports, use SWIFT MT103 for ordinary invoice settlements, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (MT700) for large or high-value lots, and documentary collections under URC 522 for trusted counterparties. Payments to the China parent should be executed as cross-strait remittances with the appropriate SAFE/CBC purpose code via a Tier-1 bank, using USD, CNY, or TWD settlement according to the underlying invoice currency. Domestic bonded-transfer obligations within Taiwan are settled through the Taiwan Clearing House (FISC) or direct interbank transfer, while the bonded warehouse inventory movement is separately recorded under customs supervision; this is an inventory-control event, not a standalone payment rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable USD/TWD and EUR/TWD forward contracts, tenor up to 12 months, only against documented bonded trade invoices or committed purchase orders for Bordeaux wine and Scotch whisky.

Cross-currency forwards and currency swaps between TWD and USD, EUR, or GBP for genuine commercial hedging of import payables and intercompany settlement, provided the underlying position is evidenced by contracts and the CBC-designated FX bank confirms the real-demand principle.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts are not permissible for onshore New Taiwan dollar exposure; TWD hedging must be executed as onshore deliverable forwards. China-side parent treasury operations may hedge CNY exposure through CNH/USD deliverable forwards or offshore CNH NDFs, but those instruments cannot be booked by the Taiwan WFOE for TWD conversion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and Financial Statement Attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (competent local district office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May for calendar-year profit-seeking enterprises; within five months after the approved special fiscal year-end for non-calendar-year filers; payment of the self-assessed tax is due on the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled returns trigger estimated assessment, a 10% additional tax on the assessed unpaid liability, daily delinquency interest under the Tax Collection Act, and compulsory collection; for bonded wine/spirits traders, customs may also suspend bonded transfer permits and the Ministry of Finance may revoke the alcohol-related license for persistent noncompliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (competent local district office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing and payment by the 15th day of the succeeding odd-numbered month for every two-month period: 15 March, 15 May, 15 July, 15 September, 15 November and 15 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a surcharge of 1% per two-day period up to 15% plus interest; late filing attracts fixed administrative fines and, where tax is understated, a 5% per-month penalty up to 15% of the underpaid tax; repeated noncompliance may cause suspension of bonded transfer privileges and customs supervised movement permits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Statutory Financial Statements Approval Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Companies Registration Office (central competent company registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be convened within six months after the fiscal year-end (no later than 30 June for a calendar-year company); approved financial statements, appropriation proposals and meeting minutes must be filed with the Companies Registration Office within fifteen days after the meeting concludes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible persons are subject to per-infraction fines of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000; failure to cure after a competent authority order may lead to administrative dissolution, the Taiwanese strike-off equivalent, under Company Act Article 10, and loss of capacity to operate the bonded warehouse license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Status and Shareholding Change Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any transfer of foreign-owner shares, capital change, or change in ultimate beneficial owner must be reported within 30 days of the event; an annual foreign investment status and operation confirmation, where scheduled in the approval letter, is due by 31 March for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting may suspend or jeopardize the foreign investment approval, prevent the share transfer from being registered in the shareholders register, restrict profit/royalty remittance and capital repatriation, and expose the investor to administrative rectification orders and fines under the Foreign Investment Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bonded Warehouse Annual Inventory Reconciliation and Customs Duty Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance (contracting district customs office supervising the bonded warehouse)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual bonded goods stocktaking and inventory reconciliation return must be submitted by 31 January after the close of the preceding calendar year; daily or transactional movement records for wines and spirits must remain current in the bonded goods electronic system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inventory shortages not supported by valid duty-paid or export documentation are treated as smuggled items and assessed import duty, tobacco/alcohol excise taxes and fines up to five times the duty due; severe or repeated imbalances trigger revocation of the bonded warehouse registration and immediate cessation of bonded wine/spirits wholesale trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tobacco and Alcohol Trader Annual Self-Declaration and License Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tobacco and Alcohol Administration, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual self-declaration of alcohol purchase, sales, bonded aging inventory and destruction quantities is due by 31 January after the close of the preceding calendar year; the bonded warehouse and alcohol distribution license status must be maintained and renewed before expiry, with periodic supervisory verification typically every three years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violations attract administrative fines of NT$30,000 to NT$150,000 per offense; failure to file the annual self-declaration or maintain current licensing records may suspend the alcohol trader license, terminate bonded status, and expose the company to additional customs and tax collection measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified public accountant audit of annual financial statements is mandatory in Taiwan for a non-public limited company when any of the following quantitative or legal triggers is met: (i) paid-in capital equals or exceeds NT$30 million (approximately USD 938,000); (ii) annual net revenue equals or exceeds NT$100 million (approximately USD 3.13 million); (iii) average full-time employees exceed 100 persons in the relevant annual compliance assessment; (iv) the company is a public company, bank, financial holding company, securities firm, insurance company, or another entity supervised by the Financial Supervisory Commission; (v) the company is a bonded warehouse operator or tobacco/alcohol importer and the Ministry of Finance or Customs Administration requires CPA-attested inventory, financial or fiduciary statements; or (vi) the company voluntarily or by tax authority requirement files a certified profit-seeking enterprise income tax return under the Income Tax Act attestation rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements are governed by the Business Entity Accounting Act, the Regulations on Uniform Accounting System for Business Entities, and, for public issuers, Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TIFRS). Non-public WFOE entities commonly apply Taiwan IFRS-compliant Enterprise Accounting Standards or SME-oriented ROC GAAP principles, with customs and tobacco/alcohol valuations following the Customs Valuation Regulations and the duty schedules under the Tobacco and Alcohol Administration Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a separate annual UBO registry filing for ordinary private WFOEs, but the Company Act rules require the shareholder register to be current and physically kept at the registered office; share transfers, pledges and ultimate beneficial ownership changes must be reported to the company registry and, for foreign-invested companies, to the Investment Commission within 30 days of the event. In practice, the WFOE must re-confirm UBO information annually by (i) submitting the foreign investment annual status report to the Investment Commission by 31 March, (ii) providing certified ownership schedules with the 31 May tax return, (iii) completing the annual AML/KYC review with its Taiwanese banking and customs counterparts, and (iv) attaching the updated beneficial ownership certificate to bonded warehouse customs account documentation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders and Board Meetings
Bonded Warehouse Inventory Ledger and Duty-Status Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - 2,500 per annum covering registered office, registered agent, corporate secretarial services and local compliance coordination in Taiwan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 12,000 per annum for CPA audit, certification of annual financial statements and bonded inventory attestation depending on trade volume and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan applies a 20% statutory rate to profit-seeking enterprises. Qualifying Free Trade Zone (FTZ) enterprises may claim a corporate income tax exemption on qualifying offshore trading profits derived from bonded logistics activities under Article 25 of the Free Trade Zone Act. R&D investment credits up to 10% are available under the Statute for Industrial Innovation. No patent box or special wine/spirit incentive applies, so the effective rate remains approximately 20% absent such credits or exemptions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form 15) filed electronically through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance National Taxation e-Filing System (電子申報)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed by May 31 of the year immediately following the fiscal year-end (i.e., within 5 months of the fiscal year close). A one-month extension is available for returns prepared by certified public accountants, subject to prior filing of a request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue: gross sales, service revenue, and rental income from bonded wholesale trade of aged Scotch and Bordeaux wines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Taiwan-source revenue. For a Taiwan-resident wholly foreign-owned entity with a Chinese ultimate parent, ensure, based on transaction documents, that revenue from bonded transfer sales completed in Taiwan customs territory is fully declared. Offshore sales, if any, that can be clearly attributed to a foreign PE outside Taiwan must be excluded only if the Cross-Strait DTA applies and prior tax authority approval is documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: customs duties, bonded warehouse storage fees, alcoholic beverage excise tax, freight, inventory write-downs, and cost adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Under the bonded regime, customs duty and alcohol tax are deferred until goods are released into Taiwan free circulation; for income tax purposes, cost is recognized only upon sale. For related-party purchases from the Chinese parent, apply the OECD Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) to verify that the cost of goods sold is at arm's length. The Taiwan TP Examination Rules require a local file supporting the pricing; if the Taiwan entity acts as a limited-risk distributor, net margin should fall within the interquartile range, otherwise the tax authority will issue an adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: payroll, rent, marketing, freight, insurance, professional fees, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses incurred to produce Taiwan-source income are deductible. Cross-border payments for management services or brand-related support to the Chinese parent must be supported by a written intercompany agreement and a valid Certificate of Significant Economic Activities (substance). If a payment is characterized as a royalty (e.g., license for trademarks or sales networks), the statutory 20% WHT applies unless the Cross-Strait DTA reduced rate of 10% is approved. Ensure that the related-party nature is disclosed on the annual related-party disclosure statement to avoid Article 110 penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income: foreign exchange gain, interest income, dividend income, rental income, and miscellaneous income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest income from Taiwanese bank deposits is fully taxable for the Taiwan resident entity. Dividend income from a Chinese subsidiary is taxable in Taiwan, but a foreign tax credit under the Cross-Strait DTA is available for China withholding tax; attach the Chinese Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and the tax payment certificate. Be alert to deemed interest income under thin capitalization if the debt-to-equity ratio exceeds 3:1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before income tax: Box 1 minus Box 2 minus Box 3 plus Box 4, adjusted for nondeductible expenses, tax-exempt income, and book-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile net accounting profit to taxable income using the reconciliation schedule. Add back nondeductible items such as fines, criminal penalties, undocumented entertainment, and disallowed intercompany charges. If the National Taxation Bureau has previously made a transfer pricing adjustment, that adjustment should be reflected in the current year.Both the managing director and the tax agent must sign the declaration that the return is complete and accurate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retained earnings surtax: 5% surtax on undistributed earnings under Article 66-9 of the Income Tax Act, calculated on the balance of unappropriated retained earnings as of the end of the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Chinese parent does not pass a shareholder resolution to distribute dividends by the end of the year, the Taiwan entity owes a 5% retained earnings surtax on the unappropriated balance. This surtax is creditable against future dividend withholding tax when the profit is later distributed. The shareholder resolution and the Chinese parent's TRC must be kept in the file to support any future refund application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alternative minimum tax (AMT) / basic income calculation: adds back certain tax-exempt or preferentially taxed income, including FTZ offshore profits, tax-exempt bond interest, and specified incentives, then applies a 12% rate if the amount exceeds the regular tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Taiwan resident company, any income sheltered by FTZ incentives must be added back to the basic income if the beneficial deduction exceeds 50% of taxable income. The Cross-Strait DTA CFC rules must be reviewed: if the Chinese parent controls a CFC in a zero-tax jurisdiction, the Taiwan entity is not directly liable, but dividends repatriated from the CFC are subject to Taiwan AMT. Submit Form 15-9 when the calculated AMT exceeds the regular CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable: tentative tax (taxable income × 20%) minus investment tax credits, foreign tax credits, prepayments, and interim withholding taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 20% statutory rate to Box 5 income. Foreign tax credits for Chinese source income are limited to the Taiwan tax attributable to the same income. The Chinese parent's reduced WHT on dividends (5% or 10%) is claimed by the shareholder at the time of distribution, not in the entity's own return. Attach China TRC and tax payment receipts to support any credit. The balance of tax payable is payable by May 31.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penalty of 3% of the underpaid tax for each two-month period, up to 9%. Late payment incurs a 1% surcharge for every two days of delay, capped at 15%. If the return is not filed, the National Taxation Bureau makes an official assessment, and a penalty of up to 3 times the underpaid tax is imposed under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act. Fraudulent tax evasion is a criminal offense under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act, with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to NT$6 million. TP concealment or failure to present a local file may add a 1x-2x penalty on the understated tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% (statutory withholding tax rate on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders under Income Tax Act Articles 88 and 73; this is the rate before any DTA reduction).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation (effective January 1, 2021), the Chinese corporate shareholder must: (1) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the State Taxation Administration of China in the format prescribed by Taiwan's Ministry of Finance; (2) execute a Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Form 5A) certifying the shareholder is the true beneficial owner and is not acting as a conduit; (3) provide the TRC and declaration to the Taiwan withholding agent before the dividend remittance date; (4) the withholding agent must file a Reduced Withholding Tax Rate Application with the National Taxation Bureau (Form V-2) before or within 10 days after the payment, and receive an approval order. The reduced rate is 5% if the Chinese shareholder directly holds at least 25% of the capital of the Taiwan entity; otherwise, the rate is 10%. The tax bureau may request audited financial statements, bank statements, and evidence of the business purpose to prevent treaty shopping. If approval is not obtained before payment, the 21% is withheld and the excess can be reclaimed by filing an amended return within 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on interest and royalties paid to non-resident companies is 20% under Income Tax Act Article 88. Under the Cross-Strait DTA, the withholding tax on interest and royalties is reduced to 10% of the gross amount, provided the beneficial owner is a China resident, the payment is arm's-length, and the relevant interest/license agreements are submitted with the same TRC and Beneficial Ownership Declaration. Royalty payments for the use of Chinese-owned trademarks, technology, or know-how in Taiwan also require an approved arm's-length royalty rate; the withholding statement (Form 50) must be filed with the district tax bureau.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$50 million per annum for intercompany purchase or sale transactions; NT$30 million per annum for other related-party transactions (services, royalties, interest). A Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required if the multinational group's annual consolidated revenue exceeds NT$30 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Under the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Act Article 12-1, the Taiwan tax authority may disregard a legal entity that lacks economic substance. For the bonded warehouse WFOE, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) must be performed in Taiwan: negotiating purchase contracts, holding inventory contracts, maintaining bonded warehouse records, issuing invoices in Taiwan, and managing customs risk. If the authority finds the Taiwan entity is a shell or conduit and that the Chinese parent makes all substantive decisions, the authority may reattribute the entire income to the Chinese parent, rendering the Taiwan filing ineffective. DTA relief is denied in the absence of commercial substance; maintenance of an office, local staff, and a separate board/minutes is mandatory. A substance file should be updated annually and include employment records, lease agreements, warehouse insurance, and a risk-management decision log.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Declaration of Bonded Wine Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of gross sales from bonded warehouse transfers by creating false invoices at lower unit values, or omitting cash payments for high-end Bordeaux and aged Scotch sales, thereby reducing Taiwan corporate income tax and the retained earnings surtax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act Article 110, the underpaid tax is assessed, and a penalty of up to 3 times the amount of tax evaded is imposed. The Tax Evasion Punishment Act Article 5 provides imprisonment of two to five years and/or a fine of NT$1 million to NT$50 million. Additionally, the Tobacco and Alcohol Administration Act may revoke the bonded warehouse license, and custom duty and alcohol tax become immediately payable with an additional penalty of up to 10 times the unpaid duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced: managing directors, CFOs, and signatory officers are personally liable for evaded taxes, interest, and penalties. The National Taxation Bureau may freeze personal bank accounts and assets, and a travel ban (blacklisting) is imposed under the Border Control Act. Criminal conviction leads to imprisonment of up to 5 years, disqualification from directorship for 5 years, and civil asset restitution. In severe cases, the court orders criminal forfeiture of personal real estate and luxury goods acquired with the proceeds of tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into intercompany purchase agreements for spirits and wines with the Chinese related party at prices materially outside the arm's-length range, or maintaining a debt-to-equity ratio exceeding 3:1 with excessive interest deductions, thereby shifting profits out of Taiwan and avoiding the 21% dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act Articles 43-1 and 43-2 and the Transfer Pricing Examination Rules, the tax authority may reassess income to the arm's-length amount; the underpaid tax is subjected to a penalty of up to 2 times the deficiency. Thin-capitalization rules disallow interest deductions on debt exceeding the 3:1 ratio. Intentional failure to file a Local File or to present documentation within the statutory request period results in a 2x penalty on the understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the transfer pricing certification, approved inflated invoices, or structured the thin capitalization are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency and penalties. The prosecutor may seek an anti-dissipation order freezing personal assets and a travel ban preventing overseas departure. Imprisonment of two to five years under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act can be imposed in tandem with breach of fiduciary duty claims under the Company Act. Directors are also personally liable to the company for damages caused by the manipulation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Trade-Based Money Laundering / False Bonded Warehouse Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the bonded warehouse to store duty-unpaid Scotch and wine for an undisclosed Chinese investor, falsifying warehouse ledgers, issuing false transfer documents to disguise product movement, or executing remittances through Swift Wires to conceal the proceeds of illicit sales and to funnel funds back to the Chinese parent as fake trade payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Control Act (AML Act) Article 15, trade-based money laundering is punishable by imprisonment for up to 7 years and a fine of up to NT$50 million. The Tobacco and Alcohol Administration Act imposes administrative fines of up to NT$30 million, cancellation of the bonded license, confiscation of duty-unpaid goods, and a 10x penalty on unpaid alcohol tax and customs duty. Customs Anti-Smuggling Act violations carry criminal sentences of 5 to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for directors who knowingly authorized or participated in false bonded warehouse declarations or money laundering. Directors are personally liable for all unpaid taxes, customs duty, and administrative fines up to NT$100 million. Under the AML Act, all personal real estate and bank accounts are subject to freezing and forfeiture; a travel ban is mandatory pending investigation. Criminal conviction results in imprisonment of 5 to 7 years, mandatory disgorgement of illicit gains, and permanent blacklisting from management positions in any Taiwan financial institution or bonded enterprise.
